about: PX-186: the memory axis's ranking comparison. One team's curated memory for the inventory fixture, recorded in this order (the order is the history: later items are newer), and twelve tasks whose goals need named items. The corpus and the gold were written before either ranking was measured: the store holds what a team's memory accumulates (near-duplicate notes of one procedure, a corrected value recorded beside the one it replaced, standing conventions and preferences that apply to every task, words shared by unrelated items, two sensitive notes and one repository fact validated at a revision the repository has left). Gold items are spread across the history (of the sixteen gold groups, nine are satisfied only by items from the older half of the history, five only by items from the newer half, two by either) and across record types (fact, decision, dependency knowledge, convention, preference, procedure, failure pattern). A gold group is a set of items that carry the same information; it is recalled when any one of them reaches the prompt.

items.content: The service retries a failed call 5 times.
Every changelog entry is a line '- INV-<ticket> <summary>'.
The staging service listens on port 8431.
Releases are approved by the platform team; their contact is plat-ops.
The inventory database is called inv_main_v2.
Write timeouts as a number of seconds followed by s, for example 3s.
Deploy: 1. tag the build 2. push the tag 3. announce in #ship
test_upload is flaky in parallel; run it with exactly: pytest -k test_upload -p no:xdist
Commit subjects start with the ticket, for example 'INV-12: add retries'.
A port file holds one number followed by a newline.
The public API version is v3.
Config files use lower-case section names such as [db] and [service].
Production runs in eu-west.
Branches are named inv-<ticket>-<slug>.
Show test output in quiet mode (-q).
Staging listens on 8431, as the deploy logs show.
The staging host is stg.inventory.internal and its port is 8431.
The metrics endpoint listens on port 9100.
The production service listens on port 443 behind the proxy.
Migrations against inv_main_v2 lock the items table; run them with --lock-timeout 5s.
Breaking API changes bump the major version; the previous version stays for 90 days.
The public API version is v4.
Before a release: bump VERSION, update CHANGELOG.md, tag, then deploy.
To deploy, tag the build, push the tag and announce it in #ship.
Deploy steps: tag the build, push the tag, post in #ship.
The upload test lives in tests/test_upload.py.
The service talks to inv_main_v2 through psycopg 3.
Timeouts in config files are integers in milliseconds (timeout_ms).
Customer order exports from staging were exposed in a shared log on 3 May; the staging port was closed for a day.
The release owner is on medical leave; release approvals go to the deputy privately.
Since the move to the new cluster, staging listens on port 9443; 8431 is retired.
Releases go out every second Tuesday.
Every text file ends with a single newline.
Keep change summaries to three bullet points.
In CI the upload test is flaky under xdist; run pytest -k test_upload -p no:xdist.
MAX_ITEMS is 500 in src/settings/limits.cfg.
Settings files under src/settings hold KEY=VALUE lines.
The release channel is beta-7.
Rollback: 1. revert the tag 2. redeploy the previous tag 3. announce in #ship
A staging deploy during the nightly backup (01:00-02:00 UTC) times out; wait until it ends.
Nightly backups run 01:00-02:00 UTC.
Database names carry a _v<major> suffix that tracks the schema major.

queries.goal: Write the port the staging service listens on today, followed by a newline, to out/staging.port.
queries.why: The port was corrected after a migration; the three older 8431 notes are the retired value.

queries.goal: Write the contact of the team that approves releases, followed by a newline, to out/release-owner.txt.
queries.why: A decision from early in the history; newer release notes (cadence, channel, checklist) share its words, and a sensitive note on the release owner must not be offered.

queries.goal: Write config/db.ini with a [db] section whose name key is the inventory database name.
queries.why: Two old items: the name and the section convention.

queries.goal: Add CHANGELOG.md with one entry for ticket 12, add retries, in the changelog format the team uses.
Write a request timeout of 2.5 seconds to out/timeout.txt in the format the user prefers.
queries.why: A user preference; a newer config convention about timeouts in milliseconds shares its words and is not what the task asks.

queries.goal: Write the exact command that runs the upload test reliably, followed by a newline, to out/upload-cmd.txt.
queries.why: Two notes carry the same command; either suffices.

queries.goal: Write the staging deploy procedure as a numbered list to out/deploy.md, with the time window when a deploy must wait.
queries.why: Three paraphrases of one procedure, and the failure pattern that names the window.

queries.goal: Write the current public API version, followed by a newline, to out/api-version.txt.
queries.why: Two curated items on one topic are a carried conflict; the newer one is current.

queries.goal: Write the option to pass when running a database migration on inv_main_v2, followed by a newline, to out/migration-flag.txt.
queries.why: A failure pattern among several database items.

queries.goal: Prepare the release for ticket 12: bump VERSION, add the changelog entry, and write the commit subject to out/commit.txt.
Write the branch name for ticket 31, add a rollback note, followed by a newline, to out/branch.txt.
queries.why: An old convention; a newer rollback procedure shares a word with the goal.

queries.goal: Set the items limit in src/settings/limits.cfg to 750, keeping the settings file format.
queries.why: A convention beside a fact about the same file.
